subject: ela
intro: Analyze word meaning, connotation, and tone.

items.prompt:
A word specific to a particular field (like 'atom') is a:
A) technical term
B) rhyme
C) title

The feeling a word carries beyond its dictionary meaning is its:
A) connotation
B) spelling
C) syllable count

Which word has a more NEGATIVE connotation?
A) firm
B) stubborn
C) steady

steps: Stubborn is negative. Key is B.

items.prompt:
Read.

The economy is in a recession, a period when business slows and unemployment rises.

'Recession' means:
A) a booming economy
B) a slowdown with rising unemployment
C) a kind of tax
items.answer: B) a slowdown with rising unemployment

steps: Defined in text. Key is B.
solution.answer: B) a slowdown with rising unemployment

items.prompt:
An author calls a plan a 'scheme' instead of a 'plan.' This word choice:
A) adds a negative, suspicious tone
B) makes it sound positive
C) changes nothing
items.answer: A) adds a negative, suspicious tone

solution.answer: A) adds a negative, suspicious tone

items.prompt:
'The river was the lifeblood of the ancient city' means the river was:
A) literally made of blood
B) essential to the city's survival
C) red in color
items.answer: B) essential to the city's survival

solution.answer: B) essential to the city's survival

items.prompt:
One article calls a new policy 'reform'; another calls it a 'power grab.' These word choices show how:
A) connotation can shape readers' opinions of the same policy
B) policies have no meaning
C) spelling matters most
items.answer: A) connotation can shape readers' opinions of the same policy

steps: Loaded words steer opinion. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) connotation can shape readers' opinions of the same policy

items.prompt:
Why do informational texts define TECHNICAL terms?
A) so readers understand field-specific words precisely
B) to make the text longer
C) to confuse readers
items.answer: A) so readers understand field-specific words precisely

steps: Precision for the field. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) so readers understand field-specific words precisely
